cover.title: Who Pays If You're Laid Off?
cover.label: UI TAX

lines.text: In 47 states, workers pay nothing for unemployment insurance.
lines.say: In forty-seven states, workers pay nothing for unemployment insurance.

lines.text: Employers pay instead, through two taxes: one federal, one state.
lines.say: Employers pay instead, through two taxes: one federal, one state.

lines.text: The federal tax is 6% on the first $7,000 of your pay. Pay the state tax on time, and a 5.4% credit cuts it to $42.
lines.say: The federal tax is six percent on the first seven thousand dollars of your pay. Pay the state tax on time, and a credit cuts it to forty-two dollars.

lines.text: That $7,000 limit was set in 1983, and it hasn't changed since.
lines.say: That seven-thousand-dollar limit was set in nineteen eighty-three, and it hasn't changed since.

lines.text: The state tax pays most of the benefits. Only Alaska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania also take a slice from workers.
lines.say: The state tax pays most of the benefits. Only Alaska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania also take a slice from workers.

lines.text: Lose your job through no fault of your own, and your state pays a weekly benefit. In 2026, top amounts range from $235 to $1,208.
lines.say: Lose your job through no fault of your own, and your state pays a weekly benefit. In twenty twenty-six, top amounts range from two hundred thirty-five dollars to twelve hundred eight.

lines.text: Most states pay for up to 26 weeks. Florida pays for as few as 12.
lines.say: Most states pay for up to twenty-six weeks. Florida pays for as few as twelve.

lines.text: And it's taxable income, though you can ask your state to withhold 10% for federal tax.
lines.say: And it's taxable income, though you can ask your state to withhold ten percent for federal tax.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: In 47 states, workers pay nothing for unemployment insurance
post.ig:
In 47 states, workers pay nothing for unemployment insurance. Employers do.
The federal tax is 6% on the first $7,000 of pay, cut to $42 per worker with a 5.4% credit. That $7,000 hasn't changed since 1983.
Only Alaska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania also take a slice from workers.
2026 max weekly benefits range from $235 (Mississippi) to $1,208 (Washington). Most states pay up to 26 weeks; Florida as few as 12. Benefits are taxable.
Sources: IRS, US Department of Labor, state agencies.
News and education, not financial advice.
